Runs in its own virtual machine with a separate Linux kernel (KVM).
Runs through gVisor's application kernel, isolated with hardware virtualization (KVM).
Runs through gVisor's userspace application kernel.
Maximum compatibility; shares the workspace host's Linux kernel.
Use the gVisor sandbox instead of a microVM?

Sandboxed (gVisor on KVM) runs gVisor's application kernel on the workspace host. The recommended level runs the environment in its own virtual machine with a separate Linux kernel, so a kernel-level flaw stays inside the VM.
Use the gVisor sandbox without KVM?
Sandboxed (gVisor) runs gVisor's application kernel without hardware virtualization. The recommended level additionally isolates it with KVM, so a flaw in gVisor is harder to exploit.

Standard Docker has lower isolation than the recommended isolation level. The container will interact with the workspace host's Linux kernel through Docker's normal namespace, capability and seccomp controls.
The workspace's agent manager does not support isolation levels yet.
